newsitem.title: INDONESIA: RTRS-Australia sells retired Nomad planes to Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia sells retired Nomad planes to Indonesia.

text.p: Australia announced on Thursday it will sell its fleet of 20 Nomad aircraft to Indonesia after the Australian Defence Force (ADF) retired the planes last year because Australian army pilots refused to fly them.

Australian Defence Minister Ian McLachlan said in a statement the sale was subject to final price negotiations and a final inspection of the aircraft, which are currently in storage at the Army Aviation Centre in Oakey in Queensland.
"Indonesia is interested in the aircraft for maritime surveillance, a role in which it already uses 18 Nomad aircraft acquired from Australia in the 1970s," McLachlan said.

"Maritime surveillance is well within the approved performance limitations on Nomad aircraft and in contrast to the demanding role the aircraft had in the ADF as general support aircraft for the army," he said in Surabaya, East Java.
McLachlan and Indonesian Defence Minister Edi Sudradjat met in Surabaya for the second annual talks between the defence ministers of the two countries.

An Australian parliamentary inquiry in May found failure to follow inspection and maintenance procedures caused a Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) Nomad to crash in 1990 during training exercises near Adelaide.
Investigators found the twin-prop plane crashed after its tail fell off during flight testing.
The ADF withdrew the aircraft from service in November 1994 after army pilots refused to fly the Australian-designed and built aircraft following a number of fatal accidents.
